fine_trace.code: static php_mb_regex_t *php_mbregex_compile_pattern(const char *pattern, size_t patlen, OnigOptionType options, OnigEncoding enc, OnigSyntaxType *syntax)
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled regex pattern '(?<=(?<A>b){0})\g<A>' enters oniguruma compilation through mb_ereg(); the pattern defines capture group A inside a zero-length look-behind and a subexpression call \g<A>.
During tune_call (before tune_tree), the \g<A> call node's body pointer is bound to the BAG_MEMORY syntax-tree node of group A, which lives inside the look-behind subtree.

node_char_len1 on the QUANT node '(?<A>b){0}' takes the lower==upper==0 branch: it reports min=0/max=0 with min_is_sure=TRUE and never recurses into the capture-group body, so the zero-length look-behind passes the simplification test.

Root cause: because ci.min==0 and ci.min_is_sure!=0, the zero-length look-behind is simplified by onig_node_reset_empty(), which frees the look-behind body subtree containing capture-group node A, while the call node still retains NODE_CALL_BODY pointing at the freed group.

onig_node_reset_empty -> node_reset_str -> node_free_body recursively frees the anchor body: the QUANT node is freed and its body, the BAG_MEMORY node of group A (with its 'b' string child), is freed via onig_node_free; the memory is returned to the allocator.

Sink: set_optimize_info_from_tree runs after tune_tree; for the NODE_CALL case the optimizer follows NODE_CALL_BODY(cn), the stale pointer to the freed group node, dereferencing freed heap memory (heap-use-after-free).

via: tune_call binds call body to mem_node

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: Matches the issue description: mbregex compilation of a pattern combining a subexpression call (\g<A>) with look-behind simplification; simplifying the zero-length look-behind (?<=(?<A>b){0}) frees the capture-group node A while the call node retains its body pointer, and the optimizer (optimize_nodes) later follows the stale pointer, causing a heap use-after-free.
